literal: Virtue considering, bears indeed the earth, behind-the-back watching-for, mean words of-one-who-speaks the-burden.
translation: Does the earth bear the heavy burden of one who watches for another's absence to speak mean words, only because she considers it her virtue to endure?
modern: அறத்தைக் கருதித்தான் இந்த பூமி, பிறர் இல்லாத சமயம் பார்த்துப் புறங்கூறிப் பேசுகின்றவனுடைய உடலாகிய பாரத்தைச் சுமக்கிறதோ?
explanation: The poet wonders why the earth continues to bear the weight of a person who slanders others behind their back. He suggests that the earth does not do this out of any respect for the slanderer, but solely because she considers it her own virtue to endure all burdens patiently. The word 'வையம்' (earth) is personified as a patient mother, and 'அறன் நோக்கி' (considering virtue) explains her motivation. This highlights how despicable backbiting is, as even the earth finds the slanderer to be an unbearable burden, carrying them only out of a sense of duty.
